messages:
priya: Opening a PRD intake: proposal name = 'tail SLA gates' — intent: give teams per-route tail-latency SLAs with automatic, transparent degradation strategies when SLOs are at risk. Problem: customers running mixed workloads see unpredictable P95/P99 spikes and want predictable user-facing latency without huge cost increases. Looking for quick sanity check on scope + acceptance criteria.

 dan: Which customers asked for this? any specific numbers?

 priya: Pilots are BrightCart (search + suggestions) and DocFlow (assistant w/ long context). Target asks: BrightCart search P99 <= 180ms, DocFlow chat P95 <= 450ms. They said budget increases must be explainable and opt-in.

 alex: Proposed mechanics: runtime monitors per-route tail and triggers a "gate" when projected miss probability > threshold. Gate actions include (in order): 1) prefer cached prefixes, 2) reduce batch wait time, 3) degrade to smaller model variant, 4) preempt long-running low-priority requests, 5) if still exceeding, return structured throttle/partial marker to caller.

 sara: Acceptance criteria draft:
- Pilot routes achieve configured tail SLA over a 7-day window (P99/P95 as configured).
- Under a 3-minute flash spike (10x baseline) end-to-end user-visible errors/truncations <= 2% for pilot routes.
- Observable cost delta <= +15% or documented opt-in that customers accept.
- SDKs can detect partial responses and surface a clear recoverability path.

 maria: Non-goals: not a replacement for cluster-level autoscaling or reserved Dedicated capacity. Not intended to fix hallucinations or content quality. Not offering cross-tenant prioritization in v1. Security note: aborted payloads must still obey audit/logging and not expose secrets; we'll label aborted responses in audit.

 josh: Edge cases to capture: long streaming sessions where a mid-stream function.call appears; requests with pinned high seq-len; cold KV cache spikes; retries causing thundering herd. Need deterministic behavior for eligible SDKs.

 alex: On streaming: I'd prefer we allow already-started streams to finish, but if the gate triggers mid-stream we add a header/event `x-tail-sla-warning` and after finishing in-flight tokens if we must cut, emit a structured trailer: `{"partial":true, "reason":"tail_sla_triggered"}` so SDKs can decide to re-request. We'll add sample SDK handling snippet in PRD.

 infra-bot: config-bot: Note: config-service needs new per-route proto `TailSlaGate {target_ms: int32, priority: enum, actions: repeated Action}` and a feature flag `tail_sla_gates`. Please include proto PR and migration plan.

 priya: Rollout proposal: pilot -> limited beta (up to 10 customers) -> GA. GA criteria: at least 2 pilot customers on paid plans running >= 3 weeks meeting SLAs, runbook approved, infra proto merged, SDK guidance published.

 dan: I'll coordinate pilot outreach. Also we should define a clear opt-in toggle per-tenant and an admin override.

 maria: I'll draft security and audit requirements; also recommend we require explicit tenant consent for automatic model fallback since that changes model surface.

 sara: I'll own the synthetic eval harness cases (cold cache, sustained 5x spike, microbursts) and acceptance test scripts. Will link to eval repo when ready.

 alex: I'll mock up partial-response semantics and sample SDK code. Also propose metrics: per-request `tail_sla_result` enum, histograms for latency_headroom, and sampling of full trace on gate events.

 priya: Who owns the PRD outline? propose sara + alex + maria. Deliverable: 1-page PRD + config proto sketch + acceptance checklist by EOW. I'll schedule a 30m review next Tue.

 josh: One more: consider tenant-level weighting so parent companies can assign higher priority to billing-critical routes later. Not for v1 but capture as backlog.

 priya: Thanks — if no objections I'll mark this intake accepted and set owners.

 dan: No objections from me.

 maria: OK.

 alex: Fine by me.

 priya: Owners set: sara (harness & runbook), alex (SDK + partial semantics), maria (security & tenant opt-in), dan (pilot coordination). PRD draft due EOW.
